title: The Three Key Resilience Risks Often Missed in Strategy Talks
summaryOrExtract: Joining the FinextraTV studio, Wayne Scott, Global Regulatory Compliance Lead, Escode described the things that underpin a resiliency discussion, growing in complexity. Scott explained how many have some idea about how to protect their software from harm, but are missing a strong focus across supply failure, service deterioration, and concentration risk. When going further into the top of concentration, Scott spoke about how leaders often use the adage 'too big to fail’ but have underestimated that many are too big to save. He said this is why resiliency is so crucial and described how, while some carry commonalities, global regulation is also extremely different. Scott defines these differences by explaining how the UK, India, Saudia Arabia, US and Switzerland approach regulation and what this might mean for finding the correct approach. At the centre of all of this, Scott emphasises the clear and evidential important of Escrow when reducing exposure and third-party risks.

title: The Future of Payments is More Than Just the Next 'Shiny New Toy'

Warsop describes the benefits of a forum to focus on how to progress payments towards a new future. He explained how the industry has a tendency to focus on the 'shiny new toy' and how payments are not forgiving, so execution has to be watertight. He describes the unfortunate reality of how conceptualisation is a lot easier than reality, and payments often runs into the struggles of this realisation - the hard work begins when the conceptual part is down and it's turned into a reality.

title: How Market Sentiment Affects Banks Innovation Opportunities
summaryOrExtract: While at Payments Unleashed in London, Philip Bruno, Chief Strategy and Growth Officer, ACI Worldwide joined FinextraTV to discuss how banks should approach innovation. Bruno, when talking about how the markets inform bank innovation, said that markets are currently quite negative towards banks, especially when it comes to price-to-book ratios. He equally described the main pitfalls of banks strategies, saying that they need to be more open to cutting losses and learning from failures, rather than sticking to plans and partners that aren't working.

title: Why Unlimited Budgets Don't Create Winning Strategies
summaryOrExtract: At Payments Unleashed in London, Fred Slevin, Global Head, Solution Consulting, ACI Worldwide, joined FinextraTV to discuss where banks often underestimate execution beyond strategies. Slevin explained how many banks are good at developing strategies, but do not effectively appreciate the requirements needed to turn strategies into actions. Slevin believes the future belongs not to the banks with the biggest budgets or the grandest ambitions, but to those with a clear plan and the ability to make it happen.

title: How Banks and PSPs Can Ensure Innovation Without Excluding Vulnerable Adults
summaryOrExtract: Joining the FinextraTV studio, Sean Tyrer, CEO and Founder, Money Carer helped to contextualise some of the key obstacles to traditional payments and banking that vulnerable adults face. Tyrer explains how, in the race to make payments faster, vulnerable adults are often left out of the equation, emphasising the need for optionality more than just assumed speed and innovation. He further describes how technologies like biometric cards and wearables are a strong way for banks and PSPs to continue evolving and innovating their offerings, while ensuring an inclusive product base.

title: Misconception or Magic: What to Know About the Modern Wealth Management World
summaryOrExtract: At the Communify Intelligence Experience, Rupert Baron, co-founder, TechnoWealth, returns to Finextra TV to unpack how the definition of wealth keeps moving and what that means for the industry. Baron argues the FCA's softening of the rules is nudging wealth management toward greater nuance rather than greater complexity, questions whether firms have truly embraced AI beyond the LLM, and reframes the great wealth transfer as a two-step process – first to the surviving spouse, statistically a woman, and only later to the next generation.

title: Why Banks Should Invest in More Orchestration for Better Security

title: How to Define Relevant Metrics for a Successful Core Modernisation Project
summaryOrExtract: Joining FinextraTV at the Temenos Community Forum 2026, Paul Weiss, Chief Transformation Officer, Regions Bank, discussed core modernisation and, crucially, how to actually measure its success. Weiss suggested starting with the reason that the transformation is necessary first, and finding clarity at that point in order to enable natural KPI's to follow. Weiss emphasised the need to see each journey as bank specific and not necessarily follow a set repeatable structure. When asked about lessons for other banks, he said they need to understand their total environment solution in order to proactively embed potential constraints into the timeline.

title: How Technology Creates a Better Human Advisory Experience
summaryOrExtract: Joining the FinextraTV virtual studio, Roshan Shetty, BFSI Public Sectors Head, Americas, Tech Mahindra and Bindhu Alvar Thiruvenkadathan, Chief Information Officer, Wealth Management, explained how the wealth management sector is currently adopting AI. Discussing the role of trust and security, they ultimately explain how technology is helping to provide humans with the individual customer details they need, faster. This technological intervention, they say, is built to match the customer needs that have outpaced advisor capabilities. Using this need for personalisation, and the capabilities of AI, they explain, actually ends up creating a deeper, human experience with advisors, by improving trust via speed and customisation.

title: Different Rails for Different Purposes: The Nuance of Simplifying Modern Banking
summaryOrExtract: At EBADay in Copenhagen, Craig Ramsey, Global Head of A2A Payments, ACI Worldwide joined the FinextraTV studio to discuss the changes in Instant Payments. Addressing growth, Ramsey said that initiatives like Wero are really taking off at speed and the crucial point now is ensuring that banks can still keep up with these changes and scale reliably. Ramsey described how different each rail looks, comparing ACH to Swift to Instant to RTGS and how each has different scales of complexities and the world, according to Ramsey, will only get more complex - it's banks job to simplify the offering.

title: The Importance of Banking Through An Empathetic Lens
summaryOrExtract: Joining FinextraTV at Temenos Community Forum, Muhammad Faisal Anwar, CTO, HBL discussed core modernisation and lessons learned along the journey. When thinking about whether core modernisation was 'just an IT problem, Anwar explained that banks falter when they don't first create a problem statement and what the core journey will solve. Equally, Anwar described the importance of empathy, explaining how employees should be regarded as ambassadors for the business, and how their satisfaction and morale are just as crucial. He went on to advise banks to see customer transactions as 'lifestyles' more than products or services - a house, a car, a holiday.

title: What's the Right Level of Friction for Pay-by-Bank?
summaryOrExtract: Joining FinextraTV at Payments Unleashed in London, Dean Wallace, Director, Consumer Payments Modernisation, ACI Worldwide discussed the evolution of pay-by-bank and some of the current obstacles. Wallace provided context to the growth, describing how many have tried to get rid of cards and pay-by-bank is perhaps the most succesful, but is still not an aggressive threat, given how ingrained cards still are. Looking at multi-rail environments, Wallace explains that the way that banks or cooperatives transition customers to new approaches and away from cards will define whether they stay loyal. He goes on to discuss the presence of friction and how some level allows a customer to feel safe, but too much will ruin the experience.

title: What is the Real Asset Thesis for Investable Conservation?
